title: Biryani Lounge in Reading Seeks Licence to Serve Food Until 4am
excerpt: The Hyderabadi biryani specialist on Wokingham Road has applied to Reading Borough Council for a late-night refreshment licence covering Monday to Saturday.
body:
• The Biryani Lounge at 89 Wokingham Road, Reading, has applied for a premises licence to serve late-night refreshments from 11pm to 4am, Monday to Saturday.
  • The application was submitted on 21 July 2026, with a public consultation period open until 18 August 2026.
  • The restaurant currently operates until 11pm on weekdays and Saturdays, specialising in Hyderabadi biryani and South Indian dishes.
  • Reading Borough Council's licensing policy generally restricts late-night food operations beyond midnight, requiring applicants to demonstrate they will not add to cumulative impact in the area.

The Application

The Biryani Lounge, a popular Indian restaurant and takeaway at 89 Wokingham Road in east Reading, has submitted an application to Reading Borough Council for a premises licence that would allow it to serve food until 4am six days a week.

According to the council's public notice, the application seeks authorisation for late-night refreshments from 11pm to 4am, Monday to Saturday. The application was received on 21 July 2026, and the public consultation period runs until 18 August 2026, during which residents and businesses can submit representations, according to the Reading Borough Council licensing register.

The Biryani Lounge currently operates from noon to 11pm on weekdays, with slightly extended hours on weekends. The proposed licence would add five additional hours of service on six nights, making it one of the latest-operating Indian restaurants in the Reading area.

"The restaurant holds a 4.3-star rating on Foodhub from over 1,000 reviews, with diners praising its "very authentic" flavours and family-friendly atmosphere."

A Growing Late-Night Scene

The Biryani Lounge's application is one of several late-night licence requests currently before Reading Borough Council. Bar Tokyo on Wiston Terrace has applied for hours extending to 3am Monday to Saturday, while The Water Tower in Tilehurst seeks to push its closing time to 12:30am on weekends. A Premier Caversham shop has also applied to extend alcohol sales until midnight.

The cluster of applications suggests growing demand for late-night dining and entertainment in Reading, a town with a large student population thanks to the University of Reading and a growing tech industry corridor along the M4.

What the Licensing Rules Say

Reading Borough Council's licensing policy takes a cautious approach to late-night food operations. The council's policy statement notes that applications for food sales beyond midnight are generally refused unless applicants can demonstrate "exceptional circumstances" satisfying the authority that granting the licence "would not contribute to cumulative impact." The policy cites crime statistics showing that post-midnight crime levels increase significantly.

However, the Biryani Lounge sits on Wokingham Road in East Reading, outside the town centre's Cumulative Impact Policy area where restrictions are tightest. Restaurants applying outside the CIP zone face a less stringent standard, though they must still address the four licensing objectives: prevention of crime and disorder, public safety, prevention of public nuisance, and protection of children from harm.

The stretch of Wokingham Road where the Biryani Lounge operates is already home to several takeaways and restaurants, including Perfect Fried Chicken, Guru, and Lankas Finest, creating an established late-night food corridor.

The Restaurant

The Biryani Lounge describes itself as "a hub for best and tasty biryanis to kill your hunger." The restaurant specialises in Hyderabadi-style biryani and South Indian cuisine, with a menu featuring dishes such as Chicken Vellulli Karam, Kodi Pulusu, Lamb Sheek Kebab, and the traditional Andhra dessert Poornalu.

The restaurant holds a 4.3-star rating on Foodhub from over 1,000 reviews, with diners praising its "very authentic" flavours and family-friendly atmosphere. It offers dine-in, takeaway, and delivery services.

Diaspora Connection

For the Indian community in and around Reading — one of the larger South Asian populations in southern England — late-night Indian dining options remain limited compared to cities like Birmingham or Leicester. A 4am licence would position the Biryani Lounge to serve post-event crowds, shift workers, and the late-night crowd that currently relies on generic fast food after most Indian restaurants close by 11pm.

What Happens Next

The public consultation period closes on 18 August 2026. If no representations are received, the council must grant the licence subject to the conditions in the operating schedule and mandatory legal conditions. If objections are filed on licensing grounds — crime, safety, nuisance, or child protection — the application would go before a Licensing Applications Sub-Committee for a hearing.

Residents and businesses wishing to comment can contact Reading Borough Council's licensing team at licensing@reading.gov.uk before the deadline.
